dialogue_quality_notes: Practical, action-oriented conversation with participants following up verbal requests by physical actions (opening window, washing, labeling, taking stove).
Minor redundant questioning: C asked about utensil ownership more than once before labeling.
Clear use of public environment updates to confirm actions; one small confusion in round 2 environment wording was resolved by later updates.
evaluation.final_reason: Practical actions settled the substantive issues: A washed shared utensils, C labeled personal utensils, and D physically took the stove; ventilation was enacted early (window/extractor). These actions removed the incompatible states about utensil ownership/cleanliness and stove access.
position_change_notes: Agent D: shifted from waiting/asking about stove availability to actually taking the stove once the shared utensils were cleaned (evidence: Turn 20 and public update).
Agent C: moved from inquiring about utensil ownership to labeling and separating personal utensils (evidence: Turns 7, 11, 19 and public update).
Agent A: accommodated others by washing shared utensils and turning on extractor, enabling stove handover and ventilation (evidence: public updates across rounds).

round_scores.evidence: B requested opening the window and then opened it; C asked which utensils are shared vs personal; D asked about waiting for the stove. No incompatible demands or refusals were expressed.

D's interest in using the stove while A still occupied it created a mild practical conflict (who uses stove and when). A removed the finished dish, released the stove, and turned on the extractor during the round, resolving access and ventilation concerns.

Shared utensils remained used and unwashed and personal utensils were not visibly labeled. C expressed intent to label and asked for respect for the distinction; A cannot label C's utensils—this introduced a minor unresolved issue about utensil ownership/cleanliness.

D asked whether the stove would be free once A finished washing shared utensils (conflicting timing/expectation). A began washing the common utensils, which de-escalated the timing/access tension but left the arrangement not yet fully confirmed until the stove was actually taken.

C visibly labeled and separated personal utensils and A washed the shared utensils; D then physically took the stove. The previously outstanding issues (utensil ownership/cleanliness and stove access timing) were settled by these actions.
Two minutes later the environment is stable: window open, extractor on, stove occupied by D, shared utensils clean, personal utensils labeled—no substantive conflicts remain.

substantive_insights: Immediate, observable actions (opening window, turning on extractor, washing utensils, labeling) effectively resolved practical conflicts more than extended discussion would have.
Unlabeled personal utensils and unwashed shared utensils constitute a persistent but easily remediable source of household tension; explicit labeling plus washing resolved the ambiguity here.
Stove access conflicts were primarily about timing; explicit confirmation and physical handover (D taking the stove) provided the definitive resolution.
